name: Gerry Adams
role: President of Sinn Féin (1983–2018), Westminster MP for Belfast West and Teachta Dála for Louth
summary: Adams is an Irish republican whose stated aim is a united, independent Ireland, to be reached through a border poll and democratic politics after the IRA's armed campaign, which he described as a legitimate response to British military occupation. His speeches combine a left-leaning social and economic programme (universal health care, wealth taxes, opposition to austerity) with Irish neutrality, support for the Irish language, equal marriage, and scepticism of EU and NATO integration.

abortion-legal.rationale: He said Sinn Féin was not a pro-abortion party and backed legislating only where a woman's life is at risk, and he later favoured repeal of the 8th Amendment; the sources point to limited access rather than abortion legal in most cases.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: In 2018 he said the use of armed actions against what he called English occupiers is still, in the given circumstances, a legitimate response.

arms-reduction.rationale: He listed disarmament among the aims of an Irish foreign policy of positive neutrality and objected to a nuclear-armed, militarised EU.

decide-locally.rationale: He said successive governments had centralised power and emasculated local democracy and promised proposals to radically reshape local authorities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He repeatedly demanded a border poll so that all citizens have their say on Irish unity, which fits a vote by the inhabitants on which state the north belongs to.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He said Sinn Féin was totally opposed to Partnership for Peace, called NATO a world policeman, and pledged to defend Irish neutrality in 2014.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He stated that equality is for everyone and that the Proclamation addresses all citizens equally, without exception.

minority-language-support.rationale: He pressed for an Irish Language Act and condemned cuts to Irish-language services and the Gaeltacht.

national-resource-control.rationale: He said Sinn Féin wanted a better deal on Ireland's natural resources and called for support of campaigns for public ownership of natural resources.

national-self-determination.rationale: He said the Irish have the right to govern themselves and called for Palestinian statehood to be recognised at the UN.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He denounced cronyism, golden circles and brown-envelope politics linking politicians to developers and businesses.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He opposed the Lisbon Treaty as a transfer of power to larger states and urged a No to the fiscal treaty, yet said Sinn Féin is not Eurosceptic and wants a European union of equal states, so his words point both ways on pooling sovereignty.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He said the Ard Fheis says no to racism and bigotry and called on the Irish to exorcise any trace of racism.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He said Sinn Féin would tell the EU/IMF it was time for a new deal and in 2015 praised Greece for saying no to austerity, though he did not call for refusing lenders' terms outright.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He said Sinn Féin is a united Ireland party and described partition as a British-imposed division to be ended.

revive-national-language.rationale: He called for a national revival of the Irish language and promised an Irish Language Act, though he did not say whether it should be the sole language of the state.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He launched Sinn Féin's Yes campaign for the 2015 referendum, calling same-sex marriage a modest and basic right of equality for Irish citizens.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He stood in solidarity with the Finucane family and Ballymurphy campaigners and said the British government must face up to its responsibilities for past abuses.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He urged the Irish government to support the campaign demanding that the foreign debt of the poorest nations be scrapped.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He argued for 'positive neutrality' and opposed Ireland's link to NATO structures, and in 2014 opposed EU militarisation; his statements concern NATO and the EU more than rival great-power blocs as such.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He called for a package of wealth taxes, taxes on profits and an end to tax exemptions on the wealthiest (2011), and said millionaires and tax exiles must pay their fair share (2007).

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 2007 he told the Ard Fheis people have a right to free and universal health care, and in 2014 he said Sinn Féin firmly stands for a national public health service.

notes: Adams has denied IRA membership; no position is taken from allegations about IRA conduct, and a relative's or the party's positions are not treated as his (no coatracks). Positions rest on his Ard Fheis presidential addresses (1984 read for context; the 1999-2014 speeches are the mature record), his 2018 interview on armed actions, and reports of his statements on abortion and equal marriage. His 1980s statements favouring a planned economy were not used because later speeches present a social-democratic programme and no statement settles the planned-economy items. Themes searched without finding a stated position: monarchy and head of state (only his objection to the 2011 state visit being premature, which does not settle any statement), church and state and religious schools, trade unions and class, federalism and regional powers, courts and elections, drugs, guns, immigration levels, climate and nuclear power, capital punishment. His Dáil speeches on the Seanad and the Dunnes Stores strike were found by search but the Oireachtas pages could not be opened by any download agent (copies via Wayback also failed), so they are not cited; backlog/blocked-sources.md tracks pages like these. Abortion is answered low: he opposed abortion on demand but supported legislating for risk to life and later fatal foetal abnormality and repeal of the 8th Amendment.
